column3: Frames deviation as a past, bounded loss of direction rather than a fixed identity.
Directly presents guidance into the upright path as an enduring placement.
Adds that attempts to misdirect others can return as self-loss.
Connects received favor with refusing to support wrongdoing.
Supplies the mercy setting that precedes the requested path and its exclusions.
Offers only a remote replacement-and-boundary parallel to the exclusions.
Keeps compassionate concern alongside an unsoftened diagnosis of deviation.
Places dependence and worship immediately before the request and route distinction.
Shows misdirection as enacted through inducement, command, and altered order.
Joins persistent denial and deviation while retaining distinct readings of each.
Adds no clear route, favor, wrath, or deviation evidence for the focus.
Portrays deviation as a collective, inherited orientation despite settled practice.
Treats favor as entrusted distinction carrying responsibility, not settled status.
States the immediate petition for the upright path completed by 1:7.
Presents favor as a sustained protective condition, though broadly.
Repeats the responsibility reading of favor already supplied earlier.
Provides the praise and sustaining authority framing the path request.
Links divine anger with knowingly resisting what is recognized as true.
Adds a narrower favor-and-covenant setting already covered by earlier cards.

Offers a limited warning that ease can harden resistance.
Shows guidance as needed after false alternatives are tested and rejected.

Defines the upright path through shared devotion to the one sustaining authority.

Offers only a general pressure toward compromise at a boundary.

Provides a distant contrast between assurance and wrongful expectation.
Maintains the reciprocal non-merging of the two worship orientations.
Shows anger as grief and inquiry over a broken commitment before punishment.

Reiterates a durable worship boundary from the speaker's side.
Expands loss into disappearance and unlocatability, not merely wrong opinion.
Shows a demanded substitution resisted to preserve the source and order of guidance.
Repeats the non-interchangeable worship boundary from the audience's side.
Distinguishes recognizing anger from allowing it to become automatic retaliation.
Places anger after rejection, ingratitude, and transgression, though indirectly.
Concludes the boundary with distinct, non-combined commitments.
Shows social acceptance offered as leverage to alter an authoritative message.
Adds no sufficiently localized path, favor, anger, or deviation evidence.
Separates giving from reciprocal human indebtedness, refining one dimension of favor.
Makes benefaction accountable in use and source, not a private possession.
Shows anger as a differentiated outcome under distinct claims and responsibilities.
Names the opposing worship stance that the subsequent boundary addresses.
Shows a hostile plan rendered directionless, with loss and reversal kept distinct.
Adds no clear interpretive contribution to the focus.
Provides only a general standing-before-the-sustainer context.
Depicts deviation as attachment redirected toward rival objects of loyalty.
Shows paths obstructed and made crooked through exclusionary control.

Offers a limited boundary parallel without clarifying the focus categories.

Adds a general picture of persistent extension in error without close linkage.
Illustrates material provision but not the focus's favored-route distinction.

Combines being guided to a straight path with an upright, enduring commitment.
Shows hostile obstruction stationed against the upright path.
Sets guided and error-bound groups in parallel without collapsing their agency.
Links calf-making with divine anger and humiliation in worldly life.
Associates anger with false excuses and withdrawal from costly responsibility.
Treats guidance and later deviation in relation to clarified accountability.

Locates the sustaining authority on a straight path of governing order.
Frames movement from darkness to light through the path of the mighty, praiseworthy authority.

Marks the protected servants as beyond the adversary's effective claim.

Pairs commanding justice with being on a straight path.

Links disobedience to manifest deviation.

Combines holding fast to revelation with being on a straight path.

Explicitly connects deliberate killing with divine anger and exclusion from mercy.
Describes associating partners as going far astray.

Connects rejection and obstruction of God's way with far-reaching deviation.

Makes remembrance of favor a protection amid threatened harm.

Shows a favor from the sustaining authority averting a degrading outcome.
